2.27.4.en: St. John Chrysostom v When we come to the grace of Baptism, renouncing all other gods and lords, we confess the one God, the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. But when we confess this, if we do not love the Lord our God with all our heart and all our soul and cleave to Him with all our strength (Mk 12:30; Deut 6:5), we are not the portion of the Lord, but rather are like one set upon a kind of fence, and we suffer from those iniquities from which we fled, and we do not please the Lord to whom we fled and took refuge, because we do not love Him with a whole and sincere heart (Mk 12:30).

2.27.5.en: For this reason the prophet cries out to us, seeing similar wavering in our hesitation, when he says: "Woe to the sinner who goes two ways"; "How long halt you between two opinions?" (1 Kgs 18:21). And James the Apostle says: "A double minded man is unstable in all his ways" (Jas 1:8). So we who do not follow the Lord with a straight and perfect soul, and move among strange gods, are like one on a fence. On the one hand we behave as one who has left the strange gods who drag us down, and on the other hand our Lord does not protect us because we are unsteady and hesitant [41].

2.27.6.en: Origen v If someone dies because he was given remedies that depend on superstitions, how many have died because of these remedies? And how many have died without a remedy? With what confidence does his spirit go to God? He has lost the sign of Christ, having exchanged it for the sign of Satan.

2.27.7.en: Perhaps he will say that he has not lost the sign of Christ. Can you have the sign of Christ together with the sign of Satan? Christ does not accept joint ownership. He wishes to be the sole owner of the one He bought. He bought him at a great price (1 Cor 6:20), to be the sole owner. Will you make Him a partner with Satan, to whom you sold yourself by your sin? "Woe to those of two hearts," who in their hearts offer a portion to God and another to Satan. God is angry that Satan has a portion, and so He leaves (the heart) and Satan reigns over all of it. There is a reason for the Apostle's counsel: "Neither give place to the devil" (Eph 4:27) [42].

2.27.8.en: St. Augustine Woe to the faint heart, for it believes not, and therefore it shall not be defended. [13]

2.27.9.en: What does he mean by the faint heart? The heart that loses patience and endurance, and walks with a double mind arising from unbelief or its weakness, so that it becomes unstable in all its ways (Jas 1:8).

2.27.10.en: v He whose spirit trusts in God cleaves to God. God is faithful, and does not allow him to be tempted above what he is able to bear, but with the temptation makes also a way to escape, so that he is able to endure and does not draw back in the day of battle (1 Cor 10:13).

2.27.11.en: He who glorifies himself and not God, even if he puts on a great show such as bowing down... yet he tends to draw back and flee from the day of battle. His spirit is not faithful toward God, and therefore the Spirit of God is not with him. It is written: "Everyone who does not believe in the will of God is not defended" (cf. Sir 2:15) [Vulgate] [43].

2.27.12.en: St. Augustine Woe to you that have lost patience, and what will you do when the Lord shall visit you? [14]

2.27.13.en: The Lord Christ says: "In your patience possess you your souls" (Lk 21:19). Thus the Lord placed the possession of the soul in the virtue of patience, because patience is the root of all the virtues and their guardian. Patience is to endure calmly the evils that fall upon us from others, without bearing feelings of resentment against the one who brings them upon us.

2.27.14.en: God permits affliction to believers, but as a Father He declares His care for them, so that not one hair of them perishes; and as St. Augustine says: [Be assured, brethren, that the enemies have no power over believers except to the extent that they are negligent in their temptation and trial [44].] He also says: [When the Lord Jesus urged His martyrs to patience, He promised them that the body itself would receive complete perfection in the future without loss, I do not say loss of a member of it, but without the loss of a single hair [45].]

2.27.15.en: v One may follow in the Gospel the words of our Lord Jesus Christ: "In your patience possess you your souls" (Lk 21:19). And in another passage of Holy Scripture it was said: "Woe to you that have lost patience" (cf. Sir 2:14). Whether you call it patience or endurance or forbearance, the various expressions point to the same thing.

2.27.16.en: Let us set an anchor in our hearts, and not be much concerned with the difference of words, but let the single meaning occupy us. May we enter into the depth that the words express.

2.27.17.en: The person who is occupied with the truth that the life he walks in this world is far from his true home lives in patience wherever he is in the body here on earth. He lives in patience when he knows that he possesses an eternal home in heaven, confident that in this state he finds his happiness, which he cannot find here. He is inflamed with desire for it, and it is a good, holy and pure desire!

2.27.18.en: It is clear that patience is not necessarily in prosperity but in afflictions. No one can say that he endures patiently what is pleasant; what we bear and sustain by patience is something harsh, something bitter. Patience is not necessarily in happiness, but is exercised in misery [46].

2.28.s.en: 4. He who fears the Lord and satisfaction with the word of God

2.28.0.en: 18 They that fear the Lord will not disobey His words; and they that love Him will keep His ways. 19 They that fear the Lord will seek that which is well pleasing to Him; and they that love Him will be filled with the law. 20 They that fear the Lord will prepare their hearts, and will humble their souls in His sight. 21 They that fear the Lord will keep His commandments, and will be patient until His visitation, 22 saying: "If we repent not, we shall fall into the hands of the Lord, and not into the hands of men, 23 for as His majesty is, so is His mercy."

2.28.1.en: Those who fear the Lord do not disobey His words, and those who love Him keep His ways [15].

2.28.2.en: The Lord Christ directs His speech to all believers who love Him, and shows that the divine promise is general for all, and He makes of the heart a divine dwelling or temple. "If a man love Me, he will keep My words: and My Father will love him, and We will come unto him, and make Our abode with him. He that loves Me not keeps not My sayings: and the word which you hear is not Mine, but the Father's which sent Me" (Jn 14:23-24).

2.28.3.en: v He says: "Fear God, and keep His commandments" (Eccl 12:13). Thus by keeping God's commandments you will be strong in every work, and every work will be beyond all criticism. Therefore fear the Lord, and you will do every work well; this is the fear that you must possess in order to be saved.

2.28.4.en: Do not fear Satan. By your fear of the Lord you gain authority over the devil, and he has not the least power...

2.28.5.en: In any case, fear the works of Satan, and do not carry them out, but be on your guard against them.

2.28.6.en: There are two kinds of fear (the fear of the Lord, and the fear of Satan or of men); if you wish to do evil, fear the Lord and do not do it. Accordingly the fear of the Lord is a guarantee and power and glory. Fear the Lord and live for Him. All who fear Him and keep His commandments will live for Him [47].

2.28.7.en: Father Hermas v The proof of love is its declaration through work. This is the reason why John says in his epistle: "He that says, I know Him, and keeps not His commandments, is a liar" (1 Jn 2:4).

2.28.8.en: Our love is true if we keep our will in harmony with His commandments. He who wanders here and there through his evil lusts does not truly love God, for he opposes God in his will [48].

2.28.10.en: v Remind yourself that you must always show your prudence, through a good life and your very deeds. In the same way the sick respect physicians and look upon them as their rescuers and benefactors by deed and not by word [49].

2.28.11.en: St. Anthony the Great Those who fear the Lord seek His good pleasure, and those who love Him are filled with the Law. [16]

2.28.12.en: St. Philoxenus presents to us the word of God as a living source of the divine fear, enjoining us not to repeat it with our tongue only, but to live it in our hearts, so that divine springs burst forth within us that water the soul and turn its wilderness into a fruitful paradise.

2.28.13.en: v Let us be occupied always with the word of God, not only by repeating it with our tongues, but also by meditating on it inside our hearts, so that the tongue may speak out of the abundance of the heart...

2.28.14.en: He who is continually watered by the divine teaching yields divine fruits at all times.

2.28.15.en: The hidden secrets of the heart are declared, and appear through the conduct of the other senses and their actions [50].

2.28.16.en: St. Philoxenus v If anyone does not keep His commandments, this is evidence of his lack of love for God and His Christ; but keeping the commandments of Christ by enduring temptations even to death is the proof of love (Jn 14:21, 24; Rom 8:35-37) [51].

2.28.17.en: v God honors and glorifies him who does His will, but him who disobeys His law He dishonors (Mt 5:6; Rom 2:23) [52].

2.28.18.en: v "O taste and see that the Lord is good" (Ps 34:8)... He who has not tasted honey cannot perceive its flavor. So the word of God cannot be enjoyed by teaching alone, but we must experience the depth of the teachings of truth, and touch the love of the Lord in a personal relationship. He says: "Taste," and he did not say be satisfied, "for now we see through a glass, darkly" (1 Cor 13:12), but a time will come in which I possess what I now receive as a pledge.

2.28.19.en: By grace I can taste it with this taste in fullness of joy.

2.28.20.en: Those who cannot taste foods, and have no appetite for them, but turn away from all food with disgust, ought to present themselves to the physician, so that he may open their appetite with appetizing foods, with the addition of foods of pungent (smell) to open their appetite more and more. So it is with the word of truth: we need a living experience of it, as the Psalm says that it will kindle in you a constant desire; therefore it says: "Taste," that you may receive the blessing, from your constant sense that you "hunger and thirst after righteousness" (Mt 5:6) [53].

2.28.21.en: v Question: What is the measure of our love for God?

2.28.22.en: Answer: That the soul be enlarged beyond her strength toward the will of God, and make His glory her chief concern and constant desire [54].

2.28.23.en: v Question: How can we do everything to the glory of God?...

2.28.24.en: If we do everything according to the mind of God and His commandments, and do not seek the praise of men [55].

2.28.25.en: St. Basil the Great Those who fear the Lord prepare their hearts, and humble themselves before Him. [17]

2.28.26.en: St. Jacob of Serugh says that the enemy, the devil, and Adam fell into the same vice, that is, pride; therefore God took away Adam's glory lest he fall forever like Satan, and the Lord Christ repaired the situation by our acquiring His humility, so that His Kingdom may dwell in us.

2.28.27.en: v That compassionate One, full of good things, had pity with mercies, and took from (Adam) the glory in which he was clothed.

2.28.28.en: He stripped from him the glory in which he was robed, lest he be proud and perish finally like Satan.

2.28.29.en: He used rebuke with him as He despised him: O son of dust, you are dust and a lowly clay.

2.28.30.en: Why do you wish to snatch a place that is not yours?...

2.28.31.en: You did not stretch out the heavens alone, nor did you set in order the powers that go about in them.

2.28.32.en: The sun and the moon and all the stars do not move by you...

2.28.33.en: You are dust, do not reach for greatness; you are clay, why do you think on what does not concern you?...

2.28.34.en: Hate pride, for it is a great snare, full of death, in which the enemy fell from the beginning...

2.28.35.en: There is nothing so hated and rejected with God as the pride of him who struts in boasting [56].

2.28.36.en: St. Jacob of Serugh v The low lands are filled, and the high lands dry up. Grace is rain. Why then do you wonder if God resists the proud, and gives grace to the humble (Jas 4:6)? Therefore the saying "with fear and trembling" (Phil 2:12) means with humility. "Be not highminded, but fear" (Rom 11:20). Fear so that you may be filled; do not be proud lest you dry up! [57]

2.28.37.en: St. Augustine Let us fall into the hands of the Lord and not into the hands of men, for as His majesty is, so is His mercy [18].

2.28.38.en: St. John Chrysostom sees that David, the king and prophet, when he sinned and deserved discipline, asked the Lord that he might fall into His hands and not into the hands of men, because He is a merciful God, who knows what is for his edification and the edification of the people, and does not exaggerate the discipline. He is a wise, almighty and loving Father! But if he fell under the hand of a man, this man in arrogance does not aim at his correction, and does not seek what is for his edification and the edification of the people.

2.28.39.en: But on the great day of the Lord, the falling of the obstinate man who has determined not to repent until the last breath of his life into the hand of the Lord is exceedingly terrible (Heb 10:30), and then falling into the hands of men is counted as nothing.

2.28.40.en: v He says: "It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God" (Heb 10:31); it is written: "Vengeance belongs unto Me, I will recompense, says the Lord" (Heb 10:30)... It was said: "Let us fall into the hands of the Lord and not into the hands of men" (Sir 2:18; 2 Sam 24:14). But if you do not repent, you fall into the hands of the fearful God, and falling into the hands of men is counted as nothing. He means: when you see a man punished here, let us not be terrified by present things, but be terrified by the things to come." As His mercy, so also is His wrath" and "His indignation comes upon sinners" (Sir 5:6) [58].

2.28.41.en: St. John Chrysostom v For those who have newly entered the way of godliness, the chief exercise for their greater profit is "fear," according to the counsel of Solomon, the wisest of men: "The fear of the Lord is the head of wisdom" (Prov 1:7). But as for you who have passed your infancy in Christ, and no longer seek milk, but are able to become perfect in the inner man by the food of strong teaching (Heb 5:13-14), that is, you need the high commandments by which all the truth concerning love in Christ is fulfilled.

2.28.42.en: But you must be fully careful lest through the abundance of God's gifts you fall under a severe judgment, if you are ungrateful to the Giver (God), for He says: "For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required" (Lk 12:45) [59].

2.28.43.en: v Yes, the Lord is good, but He is also just, and it is a property of the just to repay according to desert... The Lord is merciful, but He is also fair, for it was said: "The Lord loves mercy and judgment" (Ps 100:1) [60].

2.28.44.en: v He is merciful, but He is also a judge, for the Lord "loves mercy and judgment," as the Psalmist says...

2.28.45.en: You see how wisely He grants mercy; but He is not merciful without justice, nor just without mercy, for the Lord is merciful and just (Ps 115:5) [61].

2.28.46.en: v The people murmured because there was no water. As soon as Moses said to his people: "Must we fetch you water out of this rock?" (Num 20:10), he hesitated to some degree, but for this alone he immediately received the threat that he would not enter the Promised Land, which was at that time the head of all the promises given to the Jews. When I see this man ask and not obtain pardon, when I see him not found worthy to receive forgiveness for these few words, besides so many works of righteousness, I truly perceive the severity of God in the words of the Apostle (Rom 11:22). I perceive fully that these words are true: "If the righteous scarcely be saved, where shall the ungodly and the sinner appear?" (1 Pet 4:18) [62].

2.28.47.en: St. Basil the Great Holy Scripture brought out the wrath with which God threatens mankind, not so that we may live in terror, but that, as children of God, we may perceive the blessings that we enjoy by returning to Him.

2.28.48.en: v When we read of the wrath of the Lord and His anger, we must not understand the word according to the sense of an ignoble human emotion, but in a sense that befits God, who is above every passion or blemish. Hence we must perceive from this that He is the Judge and the Avenger of all the unjust things that are committed in this world.

2.28.49.en: And by the logic of these terms and their meaning, we must fear Him as the One to be feared who repays us for our works, and we must fear to do anything against His will. For human nature is accustomed to fear those whom it knows to be angry, and is alarmed at offending them, as is the case with some judges who have reached the height of justice.

2.28.50.en: The avenging wrath is usually feared by those who are tormented by the accusation of their consciences, though of course not because this inclination exists in the minds of those who will adhere to fairness in their judgments. But while they are in the midst of this fear, the judge's inclinations toward them are marked by justice and impartiality and respect for the law that he carries out. And this, however gently and kindly he acts, is branded with the harshest epithets of anger and fierce wrath by those who were punished rightly and fairly [63].

2.28.51.en: St. John Cassian v You find many passages in Holy Scripture in which God is likened to the attributes of man. So if you ever hear the words "the wrath of God and His fury," do not think that wrath and fury are emotions and attributes that exist in God, but they are a way by which God condescends and speaks to discipline His children and correct them.

2.28.52.en: For we also, when we wish to direct our children and correct their faults, appear before them in a fearful form and with a stern and firm face that does not correspond to our true feelings, but corresponds to the method of discipline.

2.28.53.en: If we showed on our faces always the forbearance and leniency that is in our souls and inner feelings toward our children, without changing the features of our faces according to the children's behavior, we would spoil them and reduce them to the worse. In this way we speak of the wrath of God; when it is said that God is angry, what is meant by this wrath is for your repentance and your correction, because God in His truth does not become angry or furious, but you are the one who will bear the effects of wrath and fury when you fall into terrible, severe torments because of your sins and evils, when God disciplines you with what we call the wrath of God! [64]

2.28.54.en: Origen v "We were by nature the children of wrath, even as others" (Eph 2:3). And Jeremiah says of this wrath: "Cursed be the day wherein I was born" (Jer 20:14). And of this wrath the blessed Job says: "Let the day perish wherein I was born" (Job 3:3). Of this wrath Job himself says again: "Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble. He comes forth like a flower, and is cut down..." (cf. Job 14:1-5).

2.29.0.en: Ben Sirach presents to us the following exercises during affliction: 1. To prepare ourselves for temptations, asking God to fix His fear in us [1], and to believe in the heavenly Savior, that He is kinder and more loving than our parents, and that He is almighty and wise. 2. To resist anxiety in distress by crying out to God [2]. 3. To fix our eyes on God and not on the temptation [3]. 4. To look at temporal life as ever changing [4]. 5. To look at God's dealings with His believers throughout history and in our own private lives [10].

2.30.s.en: Let me fall into Your hands, and not into the hands of man!

2.30.1.en: v My soul praises You and thanks You when You allow me the crucible of temptations!

2.30.2.en: You bring me into the fires of affliction, but with Your surpassing love You surround me.

2.30.3.en: With the three youths I experience the fires of the furnace, which have become dew!

2.30.4.en: Through affliction You open my insight, and I see the glory that You prepare for me!

2.30.5.en: v Your grace sustains me, and fills my depths with hope in You!

2.30.6.en: Afflictions turn into crowns of eternal glory!

2.30.7.en: In the midst of the furnace You hear the hidden thanksgivings of my heart, and You join me to the chorus of the heavenly ones.

2.30.8.en: Instead of anxiety, my soul rejoices in You, O my Savior!

2.30.9.en: v Three gifts I ask of You in my affliction.

2.30.10.en: Give my heart the spirit of strength, so that it does not faint, nor limp between two ways!

2.30.11.en: Draw me to Your pierced side, and I shall take refuge in You!

2.30.12.en: Give me heavenly wisdom, so that I may perceive what is beyond the affliction, and my faith does not weaken, nor do I lose patience, and so I become one of Your beloved in whom You delight.

2.30.13.en: v Grant me, with David the prophet and king, to cry out to You:

2.30.14.en: Let me fall into Your hands, and not into the hands of man (2 Sam 24:14).

2.30.15.en: You are truly my Father and my Savior and my only Friend.

2.30.16.en: If my father forsakes me and my mother forsakes me, You take me to Yourself!

2.30.17.en: You penetrate my heart, and You know its possibilities and its secrets.

2.30.18.en: You will not permit affliction unless it is for the edification of my soul and for the profit of many.

2.30.19.en: You are all-wise; all that You permit is for my salvation and the salvation of my brethren.

2.30.20.en: By Your fiery Spirit You continually renew my nature; You pour out Your radiance on my depths in the midst of the fires of temptations.

2.30.21.en: You shape my depths, and I become a living icon of You.

2.30.22.en: You adorn me, and the heavenly orders take pride in Your work in me.
